subject: EU data residency & VPC connectivity — contract language and evidence
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@cardiahealth.io>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cardiahealth.io>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Question: EU-only processing + VPC peering for PHI

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this. We are evaluating Redwood for a pilot that will involve patient-identifiable data in the EU. Two quick questions up front so procurement and security can triage:

1) Can you commit contractually to process CardiaHealth data (including model inputs and logs) only within EU regions? Procurement is asking for explicit language — "data will not be transferred outside the European Economic Area" — and we need to understand any failover behavior.

2) For private connectivity: can you support VPC peering (customer VPC <-> Redwood private subnet) or a private connector with no public internet egress? We need details on encryption, KMS control (customer-managed keys), and whether audit logs can be sent to our SIEM without leaving EU.

Also: please include SOC 2 evidence and your current subprocessor list. If you have a SIG/CAIQ or answers to our DPIA questions, that would accelerate procurement.

Would prefer a quick technical call this week.

Best,
Jordan
Director of IT Security
CardiaHealth

--
Attachment: none (initial ask)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@cardiahealth.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T12:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Question: EU-only processing + VPC peering for PHI

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear summary. Short answers first, then attachments and next steps: 

• Residency: Redwood can be contracted to operate in EU-only regions for hosted and private deployments. For Hosted API customers we provide an EU region with region-locking and routing policies; for stricter requirements we offer Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) which gives a private control plane and keeps workloads in your VPC or our EU-only subnet. Contract language can be provided to reflect "no transfers outside the EEA" for the covered processing activities.

• Connectivity & keys: We support private connectivity patterns (VPC peering, PrivateLink-style connectors, customer-managed VPNs). Customer-managed KMS is supported for Private deployments; hosted customers can use customer-managed KMS via dedicated tenancy. Audit logs and metrics can be exported to a customer-owned S3/GCS in an EU region or pushed to a SIEM endpoint over private network paths.

• Evidence: attaching our SOC 2 report and our standard DPA with SCCs. Rishi is copied to provide the technical breakdown and to propose a short call to map your DPIA/technical requirements. Laura is on copy for legal redlines.

Next steps: please confirm 1) whether you need pure EU-hosted (hosted EU region) or Private (VPC/on-prem) + 2) preferred times for a technical + legal sync. If you want, we can also return a redlined DPA that includes the "EEA-only processing" clause.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2026-06.pdf (stub), Standard_DPA_SCCs_2026.docx (stub)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@cardiahealth.io>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T08:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Question: EU-only processing + VPC peering for PHI

Jordan — quick technical note from the infra side (happy to run a deeper tech call):

• Routing & region lock: Redwood's Smart Routing policy can enforce EU-only execution by routing all requests to EU-serving clusters. For Private deployments we can pin model versions to EU-only hosts and disable cross-region failover. There is a documented fallback policy (we can disable automatic fallback to non-EU capacity if you need a strict guarantee).

• Network topology options:
  - VPC peering / PrivateLink: direct peering between CardiaHealth VPC and Redwood private subnet (no public egress).
  - Customer VPN or direct connect: for on-prem connectivity.
  - Dedicated tenancy (reserved capacity): isolates compute and KV caches to your tenancy.

• KMS & encryption: Support for Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) is available for Private and Dedicated. Hosted customers can use Customer-Managed KMS when purchasing dedicated capacity. All in-transit and at-rest AES-256/GCM by default; we can provide HSM-backed keys on request.

• Logging & proofs: Audit logs (token-level traces, model+route ID, timestamps) can be exported to an EU bucket or SIEM via private transfer. We can also provide sample log extracts for the DPIA.

Attachment: VPC_Connectivity_Options.md (network diagrams and expected latency ranges). Happy to set up a 60-minute architecture session; proposed slots in the HubSpot invite.

— Rishi
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@cardiahealth.io>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cardiahealth.io>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T14:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Question: EU-only processing + VPC peering for PHI

Thanks Vanessa & Rishi — that helps. A couple of follow-ups so procurement and legal can close this fast:

1) Contract language: can you provide the exact DPA clause you propose for "EEA-only processing"? Procurement will want to include it verbatim.

2) Subprocessors: can you confirm whether any subprocessors (metrics, logging, observability, or model hosting infra) are based in the US or route data through US services? If so, we need a mitigation plan and the current subprocessor list.

3) SIG/CAIQ: procurement prefers a SIG Lite or CAIQ answers to map to our questionnaire. Can you complete the sig questionnaire or provide the latest CAIQ export?

4) DPIA: do you have a standard DPIA template or sample answers we can reuse for our regulator?

Finally, our security team is asking about key ownership: will we be solely responsible for encryption keys (BYOK) in the Private deployment or is there any shared key escrow? Please call out the exact ownership model.

Procurement is aiming to finish vendor selection next week; appreciate any written artifacts you can share.

Cheers,
Jordan

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@cardiahealth.io>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-25T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Question: EU-only processing + VPC peering for PHI

Jordan — attaching the draft DPA with SCCs and our current subprocessor list for your review. I added suggested contract language for an "EEA-only processing" addendum; the clause is narrowly scoped to the processing activities described in the SOW and includes:

• a requirement that Redwood route and process the covered data only in EU-hosted infrastructure;
• a prohibition on automatic cross-region failover unless pre-approved in writing;
• obligations for subprocessors (notification + reasonable mitigation if any processing will occur outside the EEA);
• audit rights and a provision for sample log extracts to support your DPIA.

On keys: for Private deployments we support BYOK and provide a model where CardiaHealth controls the key material in a customer-managed KMS. Redwood does not retain access to key plaintext; any backup or escrow arrangements would be listed explicitly in the SOW.

We can also complete a SIG Lite export for you — Laura (legal) and our security team can coordinate the scope. If beneficial, we can push a DocuSign envelope with the redlined DPA so procurement can turn it quickly.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
